claim: The human heart typically has about 2 billion cardiomyocytes.
source: The human heart typically has about 2 billion cardiomyocytes (CMs) (Adler and Costabel, 1975; Laflamme and Murry, 2011), which together form the muscle layer of the heart responsible for contraction.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Adler and Costabel, 1975; Laflamme and Murry, 2011).

claim: Cardiomyocytes form the muscle layer of the heart responsible for contraction.
source: The human heart typically has about 2 billion cardiomyocytes (CMs) (Adler and Costabel, 1975; Laflamme and Murry, 2011), which together form the muscle layer of the heart responsible for contraction.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the function of cardiomyocytes.

claim: In mouse development, a bilateral group of cells in the splanchnic mesoderm specifies into cardiac precursor cells and forms the first heart field.
source: Early in mouse development, a bilateral group of cells in the splanchnic mesoderm specifies into cardiac precursor cells (CPCs) (Saga et al., 1999) and forms the first heart field (FHF).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Saga et al., 1999).

claim: Cells of the first heart field extend toward the midline to form a crescent-shaped epithelium known as the cardiac crescent.
source: Cells of the FHF then extend toward the midline to form a crescent-shaped epithelium, known as the cardiac crescent.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cardiac development morphogenesis.

claim: The cardiac crescent gives rise to the heart tube through a series of morphogenetic steps.
source: Through a series of morphogenetic steps, the cardiac crescent gives rise to a structure called the heart tube (Kelly et al., 2014; Vincent and Buckingham, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Kelly et al., 2014; Vincent and Buckingham, 2010).

claim: Cardiac precursor cells from the secondary heart field are added to the arterial and venous poles of the heart tube.
source: CPCs from the secondary heart field (SHF), which are derived from pharyngeal mesoderm, are added to the arterial and venous poles of the heart tube (Cai et al., 2003; Kelly et al., 2001; Waldo et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Cai et al., 2003; Kelly et al., 2001; Waldo et al., 2001).

claim: The first heart field gives rise mostly to the left ventricle and parts of the atria.
source: The FHF is believed to give rise mostly to the left ventricle and parts of the atria, whereas the SHF is believed to give rise mostly to the right ventricle, the outflow tract (OFT) and most of the atria (Cai et al., 2003; Galli et al., 2008; Waldo et al., 2001; Zaffran et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Cai et al., 2003; Galli et al., 2008; Waldo et al., 2001; Zaffran et al., 2004).

claim: The secondary heart field gives rise mostly to the right ventricle, the outflow tract, and most of the atria.
source: The FHF is believed to give rise mostly to the left ventricle and parts of the atria, whereas the SHF is believed to give rise mostly to the right ventricle, the outflow tract (OFT) and most of the atria (Cai et al., 2003; Galli et al., 2008; Waldo et al., 2001; Zaffran et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Cai et al., 2003; Galli et al., 2008; Waldo et al., 2001; Zaffran et al., 2004).

claim: The zebrafish heart contains only two chambers.
source: The zebrafish has a simpler heart than that of mouse and humans, containing only two chambers.
evidence: This is established knowledge about zebrafish anatomy.

claim: The successive phases of cardiomyocyte differentiation during development and their associated genetic pathways are well conserved between zebrafish and other vertebrates.
source: Nevertheless, the successive phases of CM differentiation during development, as well as their associated genetic pathways, are well conserved between zebrafish and other vertebrates (Staudt and Stainier, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Staudt and Stainier, 2012).

claim: In zebrafish, both the first heart field and the secondary heart field derive from the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: In zebrafish, both the FHF and the SHF derive from the ALPM (Mosimann et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Mosimann et al., 2015).

claim: Islet1 marks a subset of secondary heart field cells in zebrafish.
source: LIM domain transcription factor Islet1 (Isl1) marks a subset of SHF cells (de Pater et al., 2009; Witzel et al., 2012) that eventually give rise to the inflow tract (IFT) of the atrium of the mature heart.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (de Pater et al., 2009; Witzel et al., 2012).

claim: Islet1-positive secondary heart field cells eventually give rise to the inflow tract of the atrium of the mature heart.
source: LIM domain transcription factor Islet1 (Isl1) marks a subset of SHF cells (de Pater et al., 2009; Witzel et al., 2012) that eventually give rise to the inflow tract (IFT) of the atrium of the mature heart.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (de Pater et al., 2009; Witzel et al., 2012).

claim: A second set of secondary heart field cells is positive for Islet2b and Ltbp3.
source: A second set of SHF cells is positive for Islet family member Islet2b (Isl2b) and for latent TGFβ binding protein 3 (Ltbp3).
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about cell markers in the study.

claim: Islet2b and Ltbp3-positive cells become cardiomyocytes that populate the arterial pole of the heart tube and eventually contribute to the outflow tract of the ventricle in the mature heart.
source: These cells become the CMs that populate the arterial pole of the heart tube and eventually contribute to the OFT of the ventricle in the mature heart (Zhou et al., 2011; Witzel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Zhou et al., 2011; Witzel et al., 2017).

claim: Nkx2.5, Mef2c, and Hand2 promote cardiomyocyte differentiation in zebrafish.
source: Nkx2.5, Mef2c, and Hand2 are known to promote CM differentiation in zebrafish (Guner-Ataman et al., 2013; Hinits et al., 2012; Lazic and Scott, 2011; Schindler et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Guner-Ataman et al., 2013; Hinits et al., 2012; Lazic and Scott, 2011; Schindler et al., 2014).

claim: Tal1 and Etv2 repress cardiac specification at the rostral border of the zebrafish anterior lateral plate mesoderm, thereby reducing the number of cardiomyocytes in the mature heart.
source: At the rostral border of the zebrafish ALPM, Tal1 and Etv2, two transcription factors required for vascular and hematopoietic lineage specification, respectively, repress cardiac specification, thereby reducing the number of CMs in the mature heart (Schoenebeck et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Schoenebeck et al., 2007).

claim: Retinoic acid signaling from the adjacent forelimb field determines the heart field size by restricting the potential differentiation of anterior lateral plate mesoderm cells into heart precursor cells, limiting the number of atrial but not ventricular cells in the mature heart.
source: At the border between the zebrafish ALPM and posterior LPM (PLPM), retinoic acid (RA) signaling from the adjacent forelimb field determines the HF size by restricting the potential differentiation of ALPM cells into heart precursor cells, and thus limits the number of atrial, but not ventricular, cells in the mature heart (Waxman et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Waxman et al., 2008).

claim: The Hippo signaling pathway helps to define the number of cells in a variety of tissues and organs.
source: One well-characterized signaling pathway is the Hippo signaling pathway, which helps to define the number of cells in a variety of tissues and organs (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Zhou et al., 2015).

claim: In mammalian cells, Mst1/2 phosphorylate Lats1/2 in the Hippo pathway.
source: In mammalian cells, the active elements of the Hippo pathway include Ste20-like serine/threonine kinase 1 and 2 (Mst1/2, mammalian orthologs of the fruit fly, Hippo), which phosphorylate Large tumour suppressor kinase 1 and 2 (Lats1/2).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Hippo signaling pathway.

claim: Phosphorylated Lats1/2 induce the nuclear export of Yap1 and Wwtr1.
source: Phosphorylated Lats1/2 induce the nuclear export of the transcription factor Yes-associated protein 1 (Yap1) and its paralog WW-domain-containing transcription regulator 1 (Wwtr1), also known as Taz.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Hippo signaling pathway.

claim: Lats1/2 inhibits the formation of a complex involving Yap1/Wwtr1 and TEAD transcription factors by promoting the nuclear export of Yap1/Wwtr1, thereby repressing the expression of downstream target genes.
source: Lats1/2 inhibits the formation of a complex involving Yap1/Wwtr1 and the TEA domain (TEAD) transcription factors by promoting the nuclear export of Yap1/Wwtr1, thereby repressing the expression of downstream target genes (Zhao et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Zhao et al., 2008).

claim: Hippo signaling has been implicated in cardiac regeneration after myocardial injury in cardiomyocytes of the mouse heart.
source: In CMs of the mouse heart, Hippo signaling has been implicated in cardiac regeneration after myocardial injury (Lin et al., 2014; von Gise et al., 2012; Xin et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Lin et al., 2014; von Gise et al., 2012; Xin et al., 2013).

claim: Yap1 and Wwtr1 double-null mutations in mice are embryonically lethal before the blastula stage.
source: While Yap1 and Wwtr1 double-null mutations in mice are embryonically lethal before the blastula stage (Nishioka et al., 2009), it has been shown that Nuclear Yap1 induces CM proliferation in the adult and fetal mouse.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Nishioka et al., 2009).

claim: Nuclear Yap1 induces cardiomyocyte proliferation in the adult and fetal mouse.
source: While Yap1 and Wwtr1 double-null mutations in mice are embryonically lethal before the blastula stage (Nishioka et al., 2009), it has been shown that Nuclear Yap1 induces CM proliferation in the adult and fetal mouse.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge based on prior research.

claim: Mice depleted of Lats2, Salvador, or Mst1/2 using cardiomyocyte-specific Cre drivers exhibit hypertrophic growth due to an increase in cardiomyocyte proliferation.
source: Furthermore, mice that are depleted of Lats2, Salvador (Salv), or Mst1/2 using CM-specific Cre drivers exhibit a hypertrophic growth due to an increase in CM proliferation (Zhou et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Zhou et al., 2015).

claim: Hippo signaling plays a key role in cardiac proliferation in the mouse.
source: Together, these results suggest that Hippo signaling plays a key role in cardiac proliferation in the mouse.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies on Hippo signaling in mouse cardiac proliferation.

claim: Hippo signaling regulates the expression of genes that are essential for cell specification and differentiation.
source: In addition, although Hippo signaling also regulates the expression of genes that are essential for cell specification and differentiation (Zhao et al., 2008; Nishioka et al., 2009), we still do not know whether Hippo signalling plays a role in cardiac cell fate specification.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Zhao et al., 2008; Nishioka et al., 2009).

claim: lats1 knockout fish with the lats1ncv107 allele lack 10 bp at Exon 2, resulting in a premature stop codon due to a frameshift mutation.
source: Fish with lats1ncv107 and lats2ncv108 alleles lack 10 bp at Exon 2 and 16 bp at Exon 3, respectively, resulting in premature stop codons due to frameshift mutations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from genetic analysis and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing the mutation.

claim: lats2 knockout fish with the lats2ncv108 allele lack 16 bp at Exon 3, resulting in a premature stop codon due to a frameshift mutation.
source: Fish with lats1ncv107 and lats2ncv108 alleles lack 10 bp at Exon 2 and 16 bp at Exon 3, respectively, resulting in premature stop codons due to frameshift mutations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from genetic analysis and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing the mutation.

claim: lats1ncv107 knockout fish are viable with no apparent defect.
source: lats1ncv107 KO fish and lats2ncv108 KO fish were viable with no apparent defect (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on observational data from the study.

claim: lats2ncv108 knockout fish are viable with no apparent defect.
source: lats1ncv107 KO fish and lats2ncv108 KO fish were viable with no apparent defect (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is based on observational data from the study.

source: However, almost all the lats1ncv107lats2ncv108 double KO (lats1/2 DKO) larvae died before 15 days post-fertilization (dpf) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

source: We found that the number of atrial CMs, but not ventricular CMs, was significantly increased in the lats1wt(wild type)/ ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos and in the lats1ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos at 74 hr post-fertilization (hpf) (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—source data 1).

source: We found that the number of atrial CMs, but not ventricular CMs, was significantly increased in the lats1wt(wild type)/ ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos and in the lats1ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos at 74 hr post-fertilization (hpf) (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—source data 1.

evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: The Yap1/Wwtr1 reporter is active in lats1/2 double knockout embryos.
source: We found that the Yap1/Wwtr1 reporter was active in the lats1/2 DKO embryos and in the lats1/2 morphants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The Yap1/Wwtr1 reporter is active in lats1/2 morphants.
source: We found that the Yap1/Wwtr1 reporter was active in the lats1/2 DKO embryos and in the lats1/2 morphants (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent transcription is present in inflow tract atrial cardiomyocytes at 74 hours post-fertilization.
source: We next analyzed the activity of the CM reporter at 74 hpf and found that Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent transcription was present in IFT atrial CMs using the CM Tead reporter line (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The Tead reporter is active in cardiomyocytes located at the venous pole of the heart tube at 24 hours post-fertilization.
source: By examining the progeny of the Tead reporter line crossed with the Tg(myl7:Nls-mCherry) line at 24 hpf, we found that the Tead reporter was active in CMs located at the venous pole of the heart tube (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead activation during early cardiomyocyte determination.
source: Together, these data suggest that Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/wwtr1-Tead activation during early CM determination.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the reporter assay data showing Tead activation in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Inflow tract atrial cardiomyocytes originate from the venous pole of the heart tube.
source: Previous studies have shown that IFT atrial CMs originate from the venous pole of the heart tube (de Pater et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (de Pater et al., 2009).

claim: Islet1 plays an essential role in the development of cardiac precursor cells in the secondary heart field.
source: Isl1 is a SHF marker because it plays an essential role in the development of CPCs in the SHF, and because its expression delimitates the SHF as early as 24 hpf in zebrafish (Caputo et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Caputo et al., 2015).

claim: Islet1 expression delimitates the secondary heart field as early as 24 hours post-fertilization in zebrafish.
source: Isl1 is a SHF marker because it plays an essential role in the development of CPCs in the SHF, and because its expression delimitates the SHF as early as 24 hpf in zebrafish (Caputo et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Caputo et al., 2015).

claim: The isl1 transgene recapitulates the endogenous isl1 expression patterns.
source: The isl1 transgene recapitulated the endogenous isl1 expression patterns (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B) and expression was found in the IFT of the atrium at four dpf (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—source data 1).

claim: isl1 transgene expression is found in the inflow tract of the atrium at four days post-fertilization.
source: The isl1 transgene recapitulated the endogenous isl1 expression patterns (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B) and expression was found in the IFT of the atrium at four dpf (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: isl1-promoter-active cells are observed in the endocardium and epicardium at 96 hours post-fertilization.
source: isl1-promoter-active cells were observed in the endocardium and epicardium at 96 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, arrows and arrowheads), but they were absent from the arterial pole, OFT, and ventricular myocardium until four dpf (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: isl1-promoter-active cells are absent from the arterial pole, outflow tract, and ventricular myocardium until four days post-fertilization.
source: isl1-promoter-active cells were observed in the endocardium and epicardium at 96 hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, arrows and arrowheads), but they were absent from the arterial pole, OFT, and ventricular myocardium until four dpf (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by expression data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: isl1-promoter-active secondary heart field cells are increased in ajuba morphants.
source: Consistently, isl1-promoter-active SHF cells were increased in the ajuba morphants (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Ajuba restricts the number of isl1-positive cells in the secondary heart field.

evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Witzel et al., 2012).

claim: A significant number of Tead reporter-positive cardiomyocytes are positive for Islet1 in the venous pole.
source: We found that a significant number of Tead reporter-positive CMs were positive for Isl1 in the venous pole (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The number of both Islet1- and Tead-reporter-positive cardiomyocytes in the venous pole is significantly increased in lats1/2 morphants.
source: Furthermore, the number of both Isl1- and Tead-reporter-positive CMs in the venous pole was significantly increased in the lats1/2 morphants (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The number of isl1-promoter-active cells in the venous pole is significantly increased in lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos at 26 hours post-fertilization.

evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: The number of isl1-promoter-active cells in the venous pole is significantly increased in lats1/2 double knockout embryos at 26 hours post-fertilization.
source: As expected, the number of isl1-promoter-active cells in the venous pole was significantly increased in both lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 and lats1/2 DKO embryos (Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: isl1-promoter-active secondary heart field cells are significantly increased in the venous pole of lats1/2 morphants.

evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: The number of isl1-positive cells are significantly decreased in the venous pole in embryos expressing a dominant-negative form of Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead-dependent transcription.
source: To further confirm the importance of Hippo signaling in the SHF, we analyzed embryos expressing a mCherry-tagged dominant-negative form of Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead-dependent transcription (ytip-mCherry) (Fukui et al., 2014) and found that the number of isl1-positive cells were significantly decreased in the venous pole (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D and Figure 2—source data 1.

claim: Lats1/2-mediated Hippo signaling is involved in reducing the number of secondary heart field-derived cardiac precursor cells that contribute to the venous pole.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that Lats1/2-mediated Hippo signaling is involved in reducing the number of SHF-derived CPCs that contribute to the venous pole.

claim: yap1 and wwtr1 double knockout mutant embryos exhibit cardia bifida.
source: Interestingly, the DKO mutant embryos exhibit cardia bifida, which is also observed in the hand2 mutant (Yelon et al., 2000) (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D and a citation to published research (Yelon et al., 2000).

claim: The increased cardiac precursor cell number in lats1/2 mutants is due to an expansion of the hand2 expression domain in the secondary heart field.
source: Together, these results strongly suggest that the increased CPC number in the lats1/2 mutants is due to an expansion of the hand2 expression domain in the SHF.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing increased hand2 expression and increased SHF cells in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Overexpression of Hand2 increases the number of secondary heart field-derived cardiomyocytes in zebrafish.
source: Overexpression of Hand2 increases the number of SHF-derived CMs in zebrafish (Schindler et al., 2014), so we hypothesized that the increased number of CM in lats1/2 mutants is due to an increase in the number of CPCs in the SHF.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Schindler et al., 2014).

claim: In amniotes, the venous pole progenitors are located in the most caudal domain of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: In amniotes, the venous pole progenitors are located in the most caudal domain of the ALPM (Abu-Issa and Kirby, 2008; Galli et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Abu-Issa and Kirby, 2008; Galli et al., 2008).

claim: hand2 is expressed in the zebrafish lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Considering that hand2 is expressed in the zebrafish LPM (Schoenebeck et al., 2007), we hypothesized that hand2-promoter-active cells originate from the caudal end of the ALPM.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Schoenebeck et al., 2007).

claim: Caudal cells of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm migrate toward the venous pole.
source: Cell-tracking analysis revealed that the caudal cells of the ALPM migrate toward the venous pole (Figure 4A,B, and Video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-tracking data shown in Figure 4A,B and Video 1.

claim: Anterior lateral plate mesoderm cells move toward the posterior of the cardiac disc by 20 hours post-fertilization.
source: ALPM cells move toward the posterior of the cardiac disc by 20 hpf, and subsequently move anterior-laterally toward the venous pole of the cardiac tube by 26 hpf (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-tracking data shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: Anterior lateral plate mesoderm cells subsequently move anterior-laterally toward the venous pole of the cardiac tube by 26 hours post-fertilization.
source: ALPM cells move toward the posterior of the cardiac disc by 20 hpf, and subsequently move anterior-laterally toward the venous pole of the cardiac tube by 26 hpf (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell-tracking data shown in Figure 4A–C.

claim: hand2-promoter-active cells in the venous pole differentiate from the caudal anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: These results indicate that hand2-promoter-active cells in the venous pole differentiate from the caudal ALPM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cell-tracking data showing migration of caudal ALPM cells to the venous pole.

claim: Photoconverted cells from the caudal region of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm are incorporated into the inflow tract of the atrium and the outflow tract of the ventricle.
source: We found that the photoconverted cells were incorporated into the IFT of the atrium and the OFT of the ventricle (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by photoconversion data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Cells of the caudal region of both sides of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm can become inflow tract cardiomyocytes of the atrium.
source: This indicates that the cells of the caudal region of both sides of ALPM can become IFT CMs of the atrium.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the photoconversion data showing incorporation of caudal ALPM cells into the IFT.

claim: Tead-reporter-active cells are found in the entire region of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm at the 12 somite stage.
source: At the 12 somite stage (ss), the Tead-reporter-active cells were found in the entire region of the ALPM and overlapped with hand2-promoter-active cells in ALPM (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Tead-reporter-active cells overlap with hand2-promoter-active cells in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm at the 12 somite stage.
source: At the 12 somite stage (ss), the Tead-reporter-active cells were found in the entire region of the ALPM and overlapped with hand2-promoter-active cells in ALPM (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The Tead reporter is inactive in the rostral region of the posterior lateral plate mesoderm at the 12 somite stage.
source: We further noticed that the Tead reporter was inactive in the rostral region of the PLPM at 12 ss (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Hippo signaling acts upstream of hand2 expression in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: These data suggest that Hippo signaling acts upstream of hand2 expression in the ALPM and may play a role in determining CM fate in the ALPM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing Tead reporter activity in the ALPM and increased hand2 expression in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Hippo signaling may play a role in determining cardiomyocyte fate in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: These data suggest that Hippo signaling acts upstream of hand2 expression in the ALPM and may play a role in determining CM fate in the ALPM.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data showing Tead reporter activity and hand2 expression in the ALPM.

claim: The number of isl1-promoter-active and EdU-positive cardiomyocytes in lats1/2 morphants is comparable to that of controls.
source: We examined the proliferation of isl1-promoter-active cells using the EdU incorporation assay and found that the number of isl1-promoter-active and EdU-positive CMs in the lats1/2 morphants was comparable to that of controls (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The timing of EdU incorporation does not affect the results of the proliferation analyses.
source: Importantly, the timing of EdU incorporation did not affect the results of the proliferation analyses (Figure 5B), suggesting that the increase in the number of isl1-promoter-active SHF cells that resulted from the depletion of Lats1/2 is not caused by cell proliferation after the differentiation of SHF cells from the ALPM.
evidence: This claim is supported by EdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The increase in the number of isl1-promoter-active secondary heart field cells resulting from the depletion of Lats1/2 is not caused by cell proliferation after the differentiation of secondary heart field cells from the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Importantly, the timing of EdU incorporation did not affect the results of the proliferation analyses (Figure 5B), suggesting that the increase in the number of isl1-promoter-active SHF cells that resulted from the depletion of Lats1/2 is not caused by cell proliferation after the differentiation of SHF cells from the ALPM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the EdU incorporation assay data showing no difference in proliferation.

source: Interestingly, the gap length of the lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos, the lats1/2 DKO embryos, and the lats1/2 morphants was significantly shorter than that of wildtype embryos (Figure 5D,E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5D,E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: tal1 expression is decreased in the rostral end of the posterior lateral plate mesoderm in lats1/2 double knockout embryos.
source: We also found that tal1 expression was decreased in the rostral end of the PLPM in the lats1/2 DKO embryos and the lats1/2 morphants (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).

claim: hand2 expression is decreased in both anterior lateral plate mesoderm and posterior lateral plate mesoderm in yap1/wwtr1 double knockout embryos.

claim: tal1 expression is unaffected in yap1/wwtr1 double knockout embryos.

evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5D,F.

claim: The expression of gata4 is unaffected in lats1/2 double knockout embryos.

evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The expression of nkx2.5 is unaffected in lats1/2 double knockout embryos.
source: Importantly, the expression of gata4 and nkx2.5 was unaffected in lats1/2 DKO embryos and in lats1/2 morphants, suggesting that Hippo signaling mainly affects the hand2 expression domain (Figure 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The expression of gata4 is unaffected in lats1/2 morphants.
source: Importantly, the expression of gata4 and nkx2.5 was unaffected in lats1/2 DKO embryos and in lats1/2 morphants, suggesting that Hippo signaling mainly affects the hand2 expression domain (Figure 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5G and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

source: Importantly, the expression of gata4 and nkx2.5 was unaffected in lats1/2 DKO embryos and in lats1/2 morphants, suggesting that Hippo signaling mainly affects the hand2 expression domain (Figure 5G, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing selective effect on hand2 but not gata4 or nkx2.5.

claim: The expression levels of etv2 are comparable between control and lats1/2 morphants.
source: To confirm the specificity of Hippo action, we examined the expression of etv2, which is a marker for blood-vessel progenitors (Schoenebeck et al., 2007), and of hoxb5b, which is a regulatory molecule of RA signaling in the forelimb field (Waxman et al., 2008) in the LPM. The expression levels of both etv2 and hoxb5b were comparable between the control and the lats1/2 morphants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The expression levels of hoxb5b are comparable between control and lats1/2 morphants.
source: To confirm the specificity of Hippo action, we examined the expression of etv2, which is a marker for blood-vessel progenitors (Schoenebeck et al., 2007), and of hoxb5b, which is a regulatory molecule of RA signaling in the forelimb field (Waxman et al., 2008) in the LPM. The expression levels of both etv2 and hoxb5b were comparable between the control and the lats1/2 morphants (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Lats1/2 negatively regulate Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent differentiation of the lateral plate mesoderm into the secondary heart field at the boundary between anterior lateral plate mesoderm and posterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that Lats1/2 negatively regulate Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent differentiation of the LPM into the SHF at the boundary between ALPM and PLPM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing changes in hand2 expression and tal1 expression at the ALPM-PLPM boundary in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Bone morphogenetic protein signaling affects various contexts of heart development via Smad phosphorylation-dependent transcriptional activation.
source: Signaling mediated by Bone morphogenetic proteins (Bmps) affects various contexts of heart development via Smad phosphorylation-dependent transcriptional activation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Bmp signaling in heart development.

claim: Bmp-Smad signaling is essential for secondary heart field formation, first heart field-derived cardiomyocyte development, endocardium development and epicardium development.
source: Bmp-Smad signaling is known to be essential for SHF formation, FHF-derived CM development, endocardium development and epicardium development (Prall et al., 2007; Schlueter et al., 2006; Tirosh-Finkel et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Prall et al., 2007; Schlueter et al., 2006; Tirosh-Finkel et al., 2010; Yang et al., 2006).

claim: Yap1 promotes Bmp2b expression in zebrafish neocortical astrocyte differentiation.
source: Yap1 is known to promote Bmp2b expression in zebrafish neocortical astrocyte differentiation (Huang et al., 2016) and Bmp2 in mouse endothelial cells (Neto et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Huang et al., 2016).

claim: Yap1 promotes Bmp2 expression in mouse endothelial cells.
source: Yap1 is known to promote Bmp2b expression in zebrafish neocortical astrocyte differentiation (Huang et al., 2016) and Bmp2 in mouse endothelial cells (Neto et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Neto et al., 2018).

claim: bmp2b is expressed in the lateral plate mesoderm in the zebrafish embryo.
source: In the zebrafish embryo, bmp2b, but not bmp4, is expressed in the LPM (Chung et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Chung et al., 2008).

claim: bmp4 is not expressed in the lateral plate mesoderm in the zebrafish embryo.
source: In the zebrafish embryo, bmp2b, but not bmp4, is expressed in the LPM (Chung et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Chung et al., 2008).

claim: Bmp-responsive element-positive cells are found in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm at 14 hours post-fertilization.
source: At 14 hpf, BRE-positive cells were found in the ALPM (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Phosphorylated Smad1/5/9-positive cells are found in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm and eyes at 14 hours post-fertilization.
source: Because Bmps induce the phosphorylation of Smad1/5/9 (Smad9 is also known as Smad8) (Heldin et al., 1997), we examined the phosphorylation of Smad1/5/9 in the embryos at 14 hpf using immunohistochemistry. The phosphorylated Smad1/5/9-positive cells were found in the ALPM and eyes (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Phosphorylation of Smad1/5/9 is enhanced in lats1/2 double knockout embryos.
source: Phosphorylation of Smad1/5/9 was enhanced in the lats1/2 DKO embryos and decreased in the yap1/wwtr1 DKO embryos (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Phosphorylation of Smad1/5/9 is decreased in yap1/wwtr1 double knockout embryos.
source: Phosphorylation of Smad1/5/9 was enhanced in the lats1/2 DKO embryos and decreased in the yap1/wwtr1 DKO embryos (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: bmp2b expression is increased in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm and eyes of lats1/2 double knockout embryos at the 10 somite stage.
source: At 10 ss, bmp2b expression was increased in the ALPM and eyes of the lats1/2 DKO embryos and decreased in the yap1/wwtr1 DKO embryos (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: bmp2b expression is decreased in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm and eyes of yap1/wwtr1 double knockout embryos at the 10 somite stage.
source: At 10 ss, bmp2b expression was increased in the ALPM and eyes of the lats1/2 DKO embryos and decreased in the yap1/wwtr1 DKO embryos (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: bmp2b mRNA is increased in lats1/2 morphants at the 10 somite stage.
source: Consistently, bmp2b mRNA was increased in the lats1/2 morphants at 10 ss (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: bmp4 mRNA is increased in the venous pole of lats1/2 morphants at 26 hours post-fertilization.
source: Although we could not detect bmp4 in the ALPM in the early ss (data not shown), bmp4 mRNA was increased in the venous pole of the lats1/2 morphants at 26 hpf (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Hippo signaling functions upstream of Bmp-dependent Smad activation in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm during early cardiogenesis.
source: These results suggest that Hippo signaling functions upstream of Bmp-dependent Smad activation in the ALPM during early cardiogenesis.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing changes in Smad phosphorylation and bmp2b expression in lats1/2 and yap1/wwtr1 mutants.

claim: The number of Bmp signal-active cells marked by GFP in the venous pole is increased in lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos at 24 hours post-fertilization.
source: By analyzing the BRE reporter, we found that the number of Bmp signal-active cells marked by GFP in the venous pole was increased in the lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos and/or the lats1/2 DKO embryos, as well as in the lats1/2 morphants at 24 hpf (Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and Figure 6—source data 1.

claim: The number of Bmp signal-active cells marked by GFP in the venous pole is increased in lats1/2 double knockout embryos at 24 hours post-fertilization.
source: By analyzing the BRE reporter, we found that the number of Bmp signal-active cells marked by GFP in the venous pole was increased in the lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos and/or the lats1/2 DKO embryos, as well as in the lats1/2 morphants at 24 hpf (Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and Figure 6—source data 1.

claim: The number of Bmp signal-active cells marked by GFP in the venous pole is increased in lats1/2 morphants at 24 hours post-fertilization.
source: By analyzing the BRE reporter, we found that the number of Bmp signal-active cells marked by GFP in the venous pole was increased in the lats1wt/ncv107lats2ncv108 embryos and/or the lats1/2 DKO embryos, as well as in the lats1/2 morphants at 24 hpf (Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 6C,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 2A and Figure 6—source data 1.

claim: The number of phosphorylated Smad1/5/9-positive and hand2-promoter-active cells is increased at the venous pole of lats1/2 morphants at 26 hours post-fertilization.
source: Immunohistochemistry revealed that the number of phosphorylated Smad1/5/9-positive and hand2-promoter-active cells was also increased at the venous pole of the lats1/2 morphants at 26 hpf (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Yap1/Wwtr1 promote bmp2b expression and subsequent Bmp signaling.
source: These results suggest that Yap1/Wwtr1 promote bmp2b expression and subsequent Bmp signaling and that Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent Bmp signaling leading to the formation of the proper venous pole.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing increased bmp2b expression and Bmp signaling in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent Bmp signaling leading to the formation of the proper venous pole.
source: These results suggest that Yap1/Wwtr1 promote bmp2b expression and subsequent Bmp signaling and that Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/Wwtr1-dependent Bmp signaling leading to the formation of the proper venous pole.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing increased Bmp signaling in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Smad7 blocks Bmp-Smad signaling by interacting with activated Bmp type I receptors and preventing the downstream activation of receptor-regulated Smads.
source: We made use of Smad7, an inhibitory-Smad that blocks Bmp-Smad signaling by interacting with activated Bmp type I receptors and preventing the downstream activation of receptor-regulated Smads (Souchelnytskyi et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Souchelnytskyi et al., 1998).

claim: Overexpression of smad7 mRNA causes dorsalization.
source: We first showed that overexpression of smad7 mRNA caused dorsalization, demonstrating that Smad7 is essential for proper Bmp-Smad signaling, using 200 pg of mRNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: Smad7 is essential for proper Bmp-Smad signaling.
source: We first showed that overexpression of smad7 mRNA caused dorsalization, demonstrating that Smad7 is essential for proper Bmp-Smad signaling, using 200 pg of mRNA (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the dorsalization phenotype caused by smad7 overexpression.

claim: Injection of 100 pg of smad7 mRNA leads to a dorsalization phenotype in only 10% of the injected embryos.
source: Interestingly, the injection of lower concentration of mRNA (100 pg) led to a dorsalization phenotype in only 10% of the injected embryos.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data on smad7 injection.

claim: Embryos injected with 100 pg of smad7 mRNA exhibit a decreased number of isl1-promoter-active cells.
source: The injection of smad7 mRNA did not cause fragmentation of the cells (data not shown), but the embryos exhibited a decreased number of isl1-promoter-active cells in the TgBAC(isl1:GFP);Tg(myl7:Nls-mCherry) assay (Figure 6E,F and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6E,F and Figure 6—source data 1.

claim: Bmp-dependent signaling is required for cardiac precursor cell fate determination.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that Bmp-dependent signaling is required for CPC fate determination.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing decreased isl1-positive cells with Bmp inhibition.

claim: The expression of Islet1 is greatly reduced in embryos treated with DMH1 from 14 to 26 hours post-fertilization.
source: The expression of Isl1 and the promoter activity of hand2 were greatly reduced in the embryos treated with DMH1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The promoter activity of hand2 is greatly reduced in embryos treated with DMH1 from 14 to 26 hours post-fertilization.
source: The expression of Isl1 and the promoter activity of hand2 were greatly reduced in the embryos treated with DMH1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3C.

claim: The number of isl1-promoter-active secondary heart field cells is decreased in embryos treated with DMH1.

evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6G,H and Figure 6—source data 1.

claim: The number of isl1-promoter-inactive cardiomyocytes in DMH1-treated embryos is comparable to that in control embryos.

evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6G,H and Figure 6—source data 1.

claim: Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/Wwtr1-promoted Bmp2b-dependent signaling, which is required for both hand2- and isl1-promoter activity during secondary heart field formation.
source: We thus conclude that Lats1/2 restrict Yap1/Wwtr1-promoted Bmp2b-dependent signaling, which is required for both hand2- and isl1-promoter activity during SHF formation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing the effects of lats1/2 mutation and Bmp inhibition on hand2 and isl1 expression.

claim: The Hippo signaling pathway is involved in the determination of lateral plate mesoderm cell fate by promoting venous pole identity and increases in atrial cardiomyocyte number.
source: Here, we show for the first time that the Hippo signaling pathway is involved in the determination of LPM cell fate by promoting venous pole identity and increases in atrial CM number (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the collective data from the study.

claim: Yap1/Wwtr1-promoted signaling increases the size of the secondary heart field domain.
source: We show that Yap1/Wwtr1-promoted signaling increases the size of the SHF domain and that Lats1/2, by inhibiting Yap1/Wwtr1 activity, restrict it.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the data showing increased SHF cells in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Lats1/2, by inhibiting Yap1/Wwtr1 activity, restrict the size of the secondary heart field domain.
source: We show that Yap1/Wwtr1-promoted signaling increases the size of the SHF domain and that Lats1/2, by inhibiting Yap1/Wwtr1 activity, restrict it.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the data showing increased SHF cells in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: The increased number of secondary heart field cells in lats1/2 double knockout embryos may result from a change in fate determination of hand2-negative cells, which become hand2-positive cells in the boundary between anterior lateral plate mesoderm and posterior lateral plate mesoderm.

claim: lats1/2 mutants exhibit a subtle increase in the number of Islet1-positive atrial secondary heart field cells, with no defect apparent in other organs.
source: lats1/2 mutants exhibited a subtle increase in the number of Isl1-positive atrial SHF cells, with no defect apparent in other organs.
evidence: This is a summary of the phenotypic observations from the study.

claim: Hippo signaling does not affect cell proliferation during early stages of cardiac development.
source: Importantly, despite the known role of Hippo signaling in CM proliferation during heart maturation, Hippo signaling was not found to affect cell proliferation during these early stages.
evidence: This claim is based on the EdU incorporation assay data showing no difference in proliferation.

claim: Hippo signaling contributes specifically to the determination of lateral plate mesoderm differentiation.
source: Therefore, Hippo signaling contributes specifically to the determination of LPM differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing effects on cell fate but not proliferation.

claim: Hippo signaling cooperates with other signaling pathways to determine heart field formation.
source: We speculate that Hippo signaling cooperates with other signaling pathways to determine HF formation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the known complexity of heart field formation.

claim: hoxb5b expression in the forelimb field limits the extent of the heart field at the posterior border of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: For example, hoxb5b expression in the forelimb field limits the extent of the HF at the posterior border of the ALPM, cells of which differentiate into atrial but not ventricular CMs (Waxman et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Waxman et al., 2008).

claim: Signals generated in the pronephric field in the intermediate mesoderm and in the angiogenic field in the rostral region of posterior lateral plate mesoderm are important for the regulation of cell fate at the posterior heart field boundary.
source: Furthermore, other signals generated in the pronephric field in the intermediate mesoderm and in the angiogenic field in the rostral region of PLPM are important for the regulation of cell fate at the posterior HF boundary (Kimmel et al., 1990; Mudumana et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Kimmel et al., 1990; Mudumana et al., 2008).

claim: In the mouse embryo, the anterior and posterior secondary heart field cells differentiate into the outflow tract/right ventricular myocardium and the inflow tract/atrial myocardium, respectively.
source: In the mouse embryo, the anterior and posterior SHF cells differentiate into the OFT/right ventricular myocardium and the IFT/atrial myocardium, respectively (Galli et al., 2008; Verzi et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Galli et al., 2008; Verzi et al., 2005).

claim: The posterior secondary heart field in the heart field is located caudally in the mouse embryo.
source: The posterior-SHF in the HF is located caudally (Abu-Issa and Kirby, 2008; Galli et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Abu-Issa and Kirby, 2008; Galli et al., 2008).

claim: Tead-reporter activation occurs in the caudal zone of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Tead-reporter activation occurred in the caudal zone of the ALPM, and these cells were shown to become Isl1-positive, hand2-promoter-active CMs that are localized to the venous pole of the atrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data from the study.

claim: Tead-reporter-active cells in the caudal zone of the anterior lateral plate mesoderm become Islet1-positive, hand2-promoter-active cardiomyocytes that are localized to the venous pole of the atrium.
source: Tead-reporter activation occurred in the caudal zone of the ALPM, and these cells were shown to become Isl1-positive, hand2-promoter-active CMs that are localized to the venous pole of the atrium.
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay and cell-tracking data from the study.

claim: Both sides of the heart field located caudally contribute to the venous pole of the cardiac tube.
source: Both sides of the HF located caudally contributed to the venous pole of the cardiac tube.
evidence: This claim is supported by photoconversion data from the study.

claim: Mammalian secondary heart field cells have multi-potential to differentiate into endocardial cells and smooth muscle cells in addition to myocardial cells.
source: Further, mammalian SHF cells have multi-potential to differentiate into endocardial cells and smooth muscle cells in addition to myocardial cells (Chen et al., 2009b).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Chen et al., 2009b).

claim: isl1-promoter-active cells are detected in the atrial myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium, but not in the ventricular myocardium.
source: By generating BAC transgenic fish, we found that isl1-promoter-active cells were detected in the atrial myocardium, endocardium, and epicardium, but not in the ventricular myocardium.
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data from the study.

claim: The properties of zebrafish Islet1-positive secondary heart field cells are similar to those of mammalian posterior secondary heart field cells.
source: Together with previous reports, our results suggest that the properties of zebrafish Isl1-positive SHF cells are similar to those of mammalian posterior-SHF cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of zebrafish and mammalian SHF cell properties.

claim: Lats1/2-Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead signaling regulates Bmp2b expression, which is necessary for the formation of hand2-promoter-active cells in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm and Islet1-expressing cells.
source: Lats1/2-Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead signaling regulates Bmp2b expression, which is necessary for the formation of hand2-promoter-active cells in the ALPM and Isl1-expressing cells.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the data showing the relationship between Hippo signaling, Bmp2b expression, and hand2/Isl1 expression.

claim: The Tead activation signal overlaps with the Bmp-reporter-positive signal in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: We found that the Tead activation signal overlaps with the Bmp-reporter-positive signal in the ALPM.
evidence: This claim is supported by reporter assay data from the study.

claim: Hippo signaling controls bmp2b expression in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: By analyzing lats1/2 mutants and yap1/wwtr1 mutants, we show that Hippo signaling controls bmp2b expression in the ALPM.
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data showing changes in bmp2b expression in lats1/2 and yap1/wwtr1 mutants.

claim: Bmp-Smad inhibition expands the tal1 expression domain to restrict lateral plate mesoderm fate.
source: Bmp-Smad inhibition expands the tal1 expression domain to restrict LPM fate (Gupta et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Gupta et al., 2006).

claim: hand2 expression is diminished in the alk3 mutant at the 12 somite stage.
source: Interestingly, hand2 expression is diminished in the alk3 mutant, which is affected in a Bmp type I receptor 1a, at 12 ss (de Pater et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (de Pater et al., 2012).

claim: Bmp-Smad inhibition results in the suppression of hand2-promoter-activated GFP expression at 15 hours post-fertilization.
source: In our experiments, Bmp-Smad inhibition results in the suppression of hand2-promoter-activated GFP expression at 15 hpf.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the study.

claim: bmp2b expression is positively regulated by Yap1/Wwtr1, which balances the cell fate between the heart field and the blood cell field at the boundary between the anterior lateral plate mesoderm and the posterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Therefore, we conclude that bmp2b expression is positively regulated by Yap1/Wwtr1, which balances the cell fate between the HF and the blood cell field at the boundary between the ALPM and the PLPM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing the effects of Hippo signaling on bmp2b expression and cell fate.

claim: Bmp signaling is upstream of both hand2 and nkx2.5 in zebrafish.
source: It has been shown previously that Bmp signaling is upstream of both hand2 and nkx2.5 in zebrafish, and that the expression of both mRNAs is lost in Bmp signaling mutants (de Pater et al., 2012; Kishimoto et al., 1997; Reiter et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (de Pater et al., 2012; Kishimoto et al., 1997; Reiter et al., 2001).

claim: yap1/wwtr1 double mutants have reduced hand2 expression even though Bmp signaling is decreased.
source: However, we found here that yap1/wwtr1 double mutants still have hand2 expression (although this is reduced) and normal nkx2.5 expression, even though Bmp signaling is decreased.
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH and immunostaining data from the study.

claim: yap1/wwtr1 double mutants have normal nkx2.5 expression even though Bmp signaling is decreased.
source: However, we found here that yap1/wwtr1 double mutants still have hand2 expression (although this is reduced) and normal nkx2.5 expression, even though Bmp signaling is decreased.
evidence: This claim is supported by WISH data from the study.

claim: Bmp signal-dependent dorso-ventral axis formation is not dependent on Lats1/2-Yap1/Wwtr1-Bmp signaling.
source: Consistent with this possibility, Bmp signal-dependent dorso-ventral axis formation is not dependent on Lats1/2-Yap1/Wwtr1-Bmp signaling, suggesting that additional regulators of Bmp signaling are active in the ALPM.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that lats1/2 mutants do not show dorsalization.

claim: Additional regulators of Bmp signaling are active in the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Consistent with this possibility, Bmp signal-dependent dorso-ventral axis formation is not dependent on Lats1/2-Yap1/Wwtr1-Bmp signaling, suggesting that additional regulators of Bmp signaling are active in the ALPM.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observation that Bmp signaling is not completely dependent on Hippo signaling.

claim: Hippo signaling may act independently on both bmp2b expression and hand2 expression.
source: Another possibility is that Hippo signaling acts independently on both bmp2b expression and hand2 expression.
evidence: This is speculation about an alternative mechanism.

claim: The Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead signal promotes Bmp2b expression and Smad-dependent signaling subsequently defines the anterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: In summary, we demonstrate that the Yap1/Wwtr1-Tead signal promotes Bmp2b expression and that Smad-dependent signaling subsequently defines the ALPM (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the collective data from the study.

claim: Hippo signaling restricts the border between the anterior lateral plate mesoderm and the posterior lateral plate mesoderm.
source: Because Hippo signaling restricts the border between the ALPM and the PLPM, Hippo signaling may account for the restriction of SHF formation and the subsequent SHF-derived Isl1-positive IFT atrial CMs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the data showing changes in the ALPM-PLPM boundary in lats1/2 mutants.

claim: Hippo signaling may account for the restriction of secondary heart field formation and the subsequent secondary heart field-derived Islet1-positive inflow tract atrial cardiomyocytes.
source: Because Hippo signaling restricts the border between the ALPM and the PLPM, Hippo signaling may account for the restriction of SHF formation and the subsequent SHF-derived Isl1-positive IFT atrial CMs.
evidence: This is speculation based on the data showing the role of Hippo signaling in defining the ALPM-PLPM boundary.
